newsitem.title: USA: Consumer confidence at 28-year high in May.
newsitem.headline: Consumer confidence at 28-year high in May.

text.p: Consumer confidence surged this month to a 28-year high as Americans looked forward to continued economic expansion, the Conference Board said on Tuesday.
The private business research group said its index of consumer confidence surged almost nine points to 127.1 in May, from an April reading of 118.5.

"Consumers are not only upbeat about the current state of business activity, but believe the economy will continue to expand over the next six months," Lynn Franco, associate director of the Conference Board's Consumer Research Centre, said in a statement.
"Consumer projections are in sync with most of the key economic barometers, which are signalling healthy growth and only modest inflation ahead," she added.

The present situation component of the index jumped to 152.2 in May from a revised reading of 141.6 in April, while the expectations component, which has proven to be a key measure of future business activity, reached 110.3 in May from a revised 103.2 in April.
Nearly 33 percent of Americans said current business conditions are "good," up from less than 32 percent in April, according to the board.
The percentage of people who feel "jobs are plentiful" rose to nearly 36 percent in May from 31 percent in April, it said.
Additionally, almost 19 percent of U.S. consumers believe business conditions will improve over the next six months, up from 16 percent last month.
Almost 18 percent see more jobs opening up, compared with 14.5 percent in April, the survey found.

The Conference Board's new compensation survey "suggests that pay inflation will be subdued through both 1997 and 1998, with salary increases averaging 4.0 percent in all major industries," Franco said.
